title: Power Rankings: Three-way race for top spot
heading: 2011-12 Power Rankings: Week 1
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: Most impressive aspect of the best start in Heat history besides what we've seen from LeBron? In all five games, they've scored at least 23 points in transition. Miami went 20-2 last season when its running game cracked the 20s.

rankings.summaryHtml: If point differential means something to you -- and by now it really should -- it should be impressive to hear that the Derrick Rose-led Bulls now have three 40-point wins since December 2010 ... in a league with only nine such scores total in that span.

rankings.summaryHtml: Durant nearly became the first player since Air Jordan in 1986-87 to start a season with five straight 30-point games. And when KD scored only 12 in game No. 5, neither that nor or any Westbrookgate spillover stopped OKC from reaching 5-0.

rankings.summaryHtml: Maybe I'm saying so because the committee (of one) was there in person to see Denver splatter the defending champs in its season opener, but the Nuggets -- with all their speed and depth -- look as dangerous as a team can when it loses two early.

rankings.summaryHtml: After his usual Christmas dud, Dwight Howard became the first player since Dennis Rodman in 1997 with back-to-back games with at least 24 boards. No signs yet, then, of DH12 checking out to try to force Orlando to trade him. Yet.

rankings.summaryHtml: It's cold to say it out loud but undeniably true: Portland plays faster in the post-Roy era. It's early, obviously, but the Blazers have been a lot more watchable. Especially with Matthews, Felton and Crawford all scoring 20-plus against Denver.

rankings.summaryHtml: Through four games, Timmy Duncan had managed a whopping total of 36 points. Part of that, though, is that Coach Pop -- just granted entrance to the 800 Club in career wins -- is clearly pacing TD through the Spurs' favorable early schedule.

rankings.summaryHtml: Still trying to process L.A.'s failure to turn an eight-point lead with 2:11 to go into a Christmas Day win over Chicago, which made Mike Brown the first head coach to lose at home by one point in his debut since ... Vancouver's Stu Jackson.

rankings.summaryHtml: Maybe it's a touch too soon for Most Improved Player nominations, but keep an eye on Spencer Hawes. He's posted four double-figure rebound games in four outings already, after cracking double digits just 12 times in 81 games last season.

rankings.summaryHtml: Can the Clips possibly live up to expectations? The early returns suggest that some of us are getting carried away, but entertaining us hasn't been an issue. Not with the gaudy numbers CP3, Blake and DeAndre -- nearly four blocks per game -- are putting up.

rankings.summaryHtml: Two guys who were ready to get going: Kyle Lowry averaged 17.0 ppg, 9.3 apg and 6.3 rpg before his 18 assists against Atlanta, while Kevin Martin just scored 73 points on 48 shots in the first back-to-back-to-back of his life.

rankings.summaryHtml: Landing David West in free agency, at a very reasonable $20 million over two years, was an undeniable coup for the Pacers. D-West, though, has started slowly for a team that really should be 4-0, shooting 18-for-49 from the floor (36.7 percent).

rankings.summaryHtml: You already knew that the Knicks desperately need someone with a dependable floor game who can make the game easier. You simply know it better now after the ups and downs of their first four games. Baron Davis can't get healthy soon enough.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Hawks would owe it to themselves to try as hard they can to chase Dwight Howard no matter where he's from, but it'll be interesting nonetheless to see how the likes of Al Horford and Joe Johnson cope with seeing their names out there.

rankings.summaryHtml: The state of emergency triggered by the Cowboys' latest crisis will buy the reigning champs a little time locally. Not much time, though, if they keep digging deep holes and Delonte West continues to be their most dependable player on the road.

rankings.summaryHtml: Kevin Love has made shedding pounds and swishing step-back 3s look as natural as his board work. Ricky Rubio plays entire fourth quarters and surely will start soon. A return to the Marriott downtown with two-story rooms is on the horizon.

rankings.summaryHtml: Mark Jackson has seen more good than bad in his first nine days as an NBA coach with those wins over the Bulls and Knicks. Yet there's been no shortage of upheaval thanks to various issues for Curry and Ellis and a bad home loss to Sixers.

rankings.summaryHtml: Boris Diaw began the season with two near triple-doubles for the Bobcats, who came within a whisker of shocking Miami and starting out 2-0. The unavoidable question in response: Have Diaw and the Bobcats already hit their 2011-12 peak?

rankings.summaryHtml: Facing the prospect of a second successive 0-4 start, with Lawrence Frank toting a 20-game losing streak thanks to an L in his final 17 games coaching the Nets, Detroit got five guys in double figures to finally crack 90 points and surprise Indy.

rankings.summaryHtml: Sure looks like there might be something to those initially hard-to-fathom fears about the Suns -- Steve Nash's Suns -- not being able to score enough. Seven teams on this Monday awoke scoring less than 90 ppg. And Phoenix was one of 'em.

rankings.summaryHtml: Beating Philly at home enabled the rebuilding, our-kids-are-the-future Jazz to avoid their first 0-3 start since 1979-80. Only one team has a longer streak, FWIW: Milwaukee has gone 35 straight seasons without an 0-3 start dating to 1977-78.
